subproblem.title: Boundary and cone property pass from S = [[L]] × S₀ to the factor S₀
subproblem.statement:
Data:
- P, n ∈ ℕ; L ⊆ ℝ^P a linear subspace with 1 ≤ d := dim L < n; m := n − d.
- f = (f_1, …, f_d) an orthonormal family in L.
- S ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P); S₀ ∈ 𝒟_m(ℝ^P) with an integer multiplicity representation R₀ = (M₀, θ₀, ζ₀) (IMRep univ m, R₀.Represents S₀) such that μ₀ := R₀.measure satisfies μ₀(ℝ^P ∖ L^⊥) = 0.
Hypothesis (product formula): for every map ♭ : Λ^n → Λ^m with (♭α)(v) = α(f_1, …, f_d, v_1, …, v_m) (Lean: α (Fin.append f v ∘ Fin.cast _)) and every test n-form ω,
 S(ω) = ∫_L currentEval S₀ (y ↦ ♭(ω(t + y))) dH^d(t), with H^d = μHE[d].
Conclusion: (∂S = 0 ⇒ ∂S₀ = 0) and (S a cone ⇒ S₀ a cone), i.e. (BoundaryVanishes S → BoundaryVanishes S₀) ∧ (IsConeCurrent S → IsConeCurrent S₀).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (S : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n) (L : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (f : Fin (Module.finrank ℝ L) → Euclid P) (S₀ : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (n - Module.finrank ℝ L)) (R₀ : IMRep (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (n - Module.finrank ℝ L)) (hd : Module.finrank ℝ L < n), 0 < Module.finrank ℝ L → Orthonormal ℝ f → (∀ i, f i ∈ L) → R₀.Represents S₀ → R₀.measure (Lᗮ : Set (Euclid P))ᶜ = 0 → (∀ flat : Covector (Euclid P) n → Covector (Euclid P) (n - Module.finrank ℝ L), (∀ (α : Covector (Euclid P) n) (v : Fin (n - Module.finrank ℝ L) → Euclid P), flat α v = α (Fin.append f v ∘ Fin.cast (Nat.add_sub_of_le hd.le).symm)) → ∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n, S ω = ∫ t in (L : Set (Euclid P)), currentEval S₀ (fun y => flat ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) (t + y))) ∂μHE[Module.finrank ℝ L]) → (BoundaryVanishes S → BoundaryVanishes S₀) ∧ (IsConeCurrent S → IsConeCurrent S₀)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Notation. p := L.starProjection and q := Lᗮ.starProjection = I − p. H^k := μHE[k]. Λ^k := Covector (Euclid P) k. For a test k-form γ and t ∈ ℝ^P, γ(t + ·) denotes y ↦ γ(t + y).
No sibling children are used; every fact used is in scope after `import GMT.Ch07.Submission`. This includes Mathlib MultilinearMap.alternatization, ContDiffBump, euclideanHausdorffMeasure_smul₀ and euclideanHausdorffMeasure_homothety_image, and SimonGMT exteriorDerivative_apply and HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.
0. (Fixing ♭: interior product with the frame.) Let h := (Nat.add_sub_of_le hd.le).symm : n = d + m and e := Fin.cast h. For v : Fin m → ℝ^P put u(v) := Fin.append f v ∘ e, the tuple (f_1, …, f_d, v_1, …, v_m).
 - Updating v_j updates exactly one entry of u(v): Fin.append f (update v j w) = update (Fin.append f v) (Fin.natAdd d j) w, checked pointwise with Fin.addCases.
 - So, for α ∈ Λ^n, v ↦ α(u(v)) is multilinear. It is alternating, because equal entries v_i = v_j (i ≠ j) give equal entries of u(v) at distinct indices.
 - It is bounded by ‖α‖∏_j|v_j| (le_opNorm; f is orthonormal).
 - Hence ♭α := (v ↦ α(u v)) ∈ Λ^m, and α ↦ ♭α is linear with ‖♭α‖ ≤ ‖α‖. So ♭ : Λ^n →L[ℝ] Λ^m is continuous linear (LinearMap.mkContinuous), with (♭α)(v) = α(Fin.append f v ∘ Fin.cast h).
 Applying the hypothesis to this ♭ gives, for every test n-form ω:
 (PF) S(ω) = ∫_L S₀(♭ω(t + ·)) dt, where ♭ω(t + ·) := y ↦ ♭(ω(t + y)) is a test m-form, so currentEval equals S₀ applied to it.
1. (S₀ only sees L^⊥.) Claim: let γ, γ' be test m-forms with γ(y)(w) = γ'(y)(w) for all y ∈ L^⊥ and all w ∈ (L^⊥)^m. Then S₀(γ) = S₀(γ').
 Proof.
 - Since θ₀ ≥ 1 on M₀, H^m(M₀ ∖ L^⊥) ≤ μ₀(ℝ^P ∖ L^⊥) = 0.
 - Take H^m-a.e. y ∈ M₀ such that y ∈ L^⊥ and ζ₀(y) is a unit orientation of a subspace Q_y with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt m M₀ y Q_y (R₀.orients). Then Q_y ⊆ L^⊥, by the following lemma.
 (Tangent lemma.) If H^m(M₀ ∖ V) = 0 for a linear subspace V, y ∈ V and HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt m M₀ y Q, then Q ⊆ V.
 Proof:
  - Suppose z ∈ Q ∖ V. Then ρ := dist(z, V)/2 > 0, since V is closed, and m = finrank Q ≥ 1.
  - Let φ(x) := max(0, 1 − |x − z|/ρ). It is continuous with compact support, 0 ≤ φ ≤ 1, φ ≥ 1/2 on B(z, ρ/2), and φ = 0 on V.
  - For r > 0, η := η_{y,r} (x ↦ r⁻¹(x − y)) maps V onto V, so η(M₀) ∖ V = η(M₀ ∖ V). This set has H^m-measure r^{−m}H^m(M₀ ∖ V) = 0 (homothety scaling and translation invariance of μHE[m]).
  - Hence 0 ≤ ∫_{η(M₀)} φ dH^m ≤ H^m(η(M₀) ∩ B(z, ρ)) ≤ H^m(η(M₀) ∖ V) = 0 for every r > 0, so the tangent limit gives ∫_Q φ dH^m = 0.
  - But H^m⌞Q is m-dimensional Lebesgue measure on Q (isometry invariance and EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume). So ∫_Q φ dH^m ≥ (1/2)H^m(Q ∩ B(z, ρ/2)) > 0, a contradiction.
  Apply the lemma with V = L^⊥.
 - Then ζ₀(y)(γ(y)) = ±γ(y)(τ) for an orthonormal basis τ of Q_y ⊆ L^⊥, so it equals ±γ'(y)(τ) = ζ₀(y)(γ'(y)).
 - The integrands of R₀.action(γ) and R₀.action(γ') agree a.e., so S₀(γ) = S₀(γ').
2. (Lifts and test forms.) For k ∈ {m − 1, m} let lift_k : Λ^k → Λ^{d+k} be the continuous linear map
 (lift_k β)(v_1, …, v_{d+k}) := (1/k!) Σ_{σ∈S_{d+k}} sgn(σ) ∏_{a=1}^d ⟨f_a, v_{σ(a)}⟩ · β(q v_{σ(d+1)}, …, q v_{σ(d+k)})
 (Mathlib MultilinearMap.alternatization; multilinear in v, hence continuous). Its two properties:
 (L1) (lift_k β)(f_1, …, f_d, w_1, …, w_k) = β(w_1, …, w_k) for w_j ∈ L^⊥. A term is nonzero only if v_{σ(a)} = f_a for all a ≤ d, since ⟨f_a, w_j⟩ = 0 and ⟨f_a, f_b⟩ = δ_ab. The rest is Σ_{π∈S_k} sgn(π)β(w_π) = k!β(w).
 (L2) (lift_k β)(v) = 0 if v consists of d − 1 vectors from {f_1, …, f_d} and k + 1 vectors from L^⊥. Each term contains a factor ⟨f_a, u⟩ with u ∈ L^⊥, or a mismatched ⟨f_a, f_b⟩ = 0.
 The bump ϕ. Fix ϕ ∈ C_c^∞(ℝ^P) with ϕ ≥ 0 and ϕ(0) > 0 (a ContDiffBump at 0). Then c_ϕ := ∫_L ϕ dH^d > 0, since ϕ > 0 on a relatively open neighbourhood of 0 in L and H^d⌞L is Lebesgue measure on L.
 The forms Ω_β. For a test k-form β put Ω_β(x) := ϕ(p x)·lift_k(β(q x)). This is a test (d + k)-form: it is C^∞, and tsupport Ω_β ⊆ {x : p x ∈ tsupport ϕ ∩ L, q x ∈ tsupport β}, which is compact since x = p x + q x.
 Evaluation: by (L1), for t ∈ L, y ∈ L^⊥ and w ∈ (L^⊥)^k,
 (E) ♭(Ω_β(t + y))(w) = Ω_β(t + y)(f, w) = ϕ(t)·β(y)(w),
 since p(t + y) = t and q(t + y) = y.
3. (∂S = 0 ⇒ ∂S₀ = 0.) Assume BoundaryVanishes S. Since n ≥ 2, this means S(dγ) = 0 for all test (n−1)-forms γ. As m ≥ 1, it suffices to show S₀(dβ) = 0 for every test (m−1)-form β.
 Let β be a test (m−1)-form and γ := Ω_β (k = m − 1), a test (n−1)-form. We compute ♭(dγ(x)) on w ∈ (L^⊥)^m, using dγ(x)(v_0, …, v_{n−1}) = Σ_i (−1)^i Dγ(x)[v_i](v_0, …, v̂_i, …, v_{n−1}) (SimonGMT exteriorDerivative_apply) with v = (f_1, …, f_d, w_1, …, w_m):
 - Terms v_i = f_a. Dγ(x)[f_a] = (Dϕ(px)[f_a])·lift(β(qx)) + ϕ(px)·lift(Dβ(qx)[q f_a]), and q f_a = 0. Evaluated on (f_1, …, f̂_a, …, f_d, w), the first part vanishes by (L2), and the second is 0.
 - Terms v_i = w_j, i = d + j − 1. Dγ(x)[w_j] = ϕ(px)·lift(Dβ(qx)[w_j]), because Dϕ(px)[p w_j] = 0. By (L1), its value on (f, ŵ_j) is ϕ(px)·Dβ(qx)[w_j](ŵ_j).
 Hence ♭(dγ(x))(w) = (−1)^d ϕ(px) Σ_j (−1)^{j−1} Dβ(qx)[w_j](ŵ_j) = (−1)^d ϕ(px)·dβ(qx)(w).
 For x = t + y with t ∈ L and y ∈ L^⊥ this reads ♭(dγ(t + y))(w) = (−1)^d ϕ(t)·dβ(y)(w). By step 1, applied to the test m-forms ♭dγ(t + ·) and (−1)^d ϕ(t)dβ, S₀(♭dγ(t + ·)) = (−1)^d ϕ(t) S₀(dβ).
 By (PF) with ω := dγ: 0 = S(dγ) = ∫_L (−1)^d ϕ(t) S₀(dβ) dt = (−1)^d c_ϕ S₀(dβ). So S₀(dβ) = 0 for all β, i.e. S₀.boundary = 0, which is BoundaryVanishes S₀ (degree m ≥ 1).
4. (Cone transfer.) Assume IsConeCurrent S and fix λ > 0. For a test k-form γ write η^#γ(x) := λ^{−k}γ(λ^{−1}x). This is the affine pull-back by dilation 0 λ (x ↦ λ^{−1}x) used in blowUp, by multilinearity. Since dilation 0 λ '' univ = univ, currentEval (blowUp T 0 λ) γ = T(η^#γ) for T ∈ {S, S₀}.
 (a) η^# preserves "agreement on L^⊥". If γ, γ' agree on L^⊥ × (L^⊥)^m as in step 1, so do η^#γ and η^#γ', because λ^{−1}y ∈ L^⊥ for y ∈ L^⊥. Hence η_#S₀(γ) := S₀(η^#γ) also depends only on the restriction of γ to L^⊥ × (L^⊥)^m.
 (b) Scaling of slices. Let ω be a test n-form and β_s := ♭ω(s + ·). Then
 ♭((η^#ω)(t + y)) = λ^{−n}♭(ω(λ^{−1}t + λ^{−1}y)) = λ^{−d}·(η^#β_{λ^{−1}t})(y),
 since λ^{−n} = λ^{−d}λ^{−m}. By (PF) and the cone hypothesis,
 S(ω) = S(η^#ω) = ∫_L λ^{−d} S₀(η^#β_{λ^{−1}t}) dH^d(t) = ∫_L η_#S₀(β_s) dH^d(s).
 The last step is the change of variables t = λs on L: μHE[d](λA) = λ^d μHE[d](A) (Mathlib euclideanHausdorffMeasure_smul₀ or euclideanHausdorffMeasure_homothety_image), and L is invariant under scaling. Also S(ω) = ∫_L S₀(β_s) ds by (PF). Therefore:
 (∗) ∫_L S₀(β_s) ds = ∫_L η_#S₀(β_s) ds for every test n-form ω.
 (c) Testing. Let β be a test m-form and ω := Ω_β (k = m). By (E), β_s(y)(w) = ϕ(s)β(y)(w) for y ∈ L^⊥ and w ∈ (L^⊥)^m. By step 1, S₀(β_s) = ϕ(s)S₀(β); by (a), η_#S₀(β_s) = ϕ(s)η_#S₀(β). Then (∗) gives c_ϕ S₀(β) = c_ϕ η_#S₀(β), so S₀(β) = S₀(η^#β) = currentEval (blowUp S₀ 0 λ) β.
 As λ > 0 and β were arbitrary, IsConeCurrent S₀. ∎
proof_key_steps: Construct the interior product ♭ with the frame f. Approximate tangent planes of a set lying in L^⊥ up to a null set are contained in L^⊥. Hence S₀ only sees the values of a test form at points of L^⊥ on (n−d)-tuples from L^⊥.
Forms Ω_β = ϕ(p x)·lift(β(q x)) = ϕ(p x)·dt^1∧⋯∧dt^d∧q^#β satisfy ♭Ω_β(t + y) = ϕ(t)β(y) on L^⊥.
Direct evaluation of d gives ♭(dΩ_β)(t + y) = (−1)^d ϕ(t) dβ(y) on L^⊥, so S(dΩ_β) = 0 forces S₀(dβ) = 0.
Dilations scale slices: ♭(η^#ω)(t + ·) = λ^{−d}η^#(♭ω(λ^{−1}t + ·)); a change of variables on L and testing with Ω_β give S₀(β) = S₀(η^#β).

subproblem.title: Approximate tangent planes along Lipschitz maps: Y has approximate tangent space DF(u)(ℝ^k) at F(u) for a.e. regular u ∈ F⁻¹(Y)
subproblem.statement:
Let P, k ∈ ℕ with k ≥ 1, let F : ℝ^k → ℝ^P be Lipschitz (LipschitzWith K F), and let Y ⊆ ℝ^P be Borel with H^k(Y ∩ C) < ∞ for every compact C, where H^k = μHE[k].
Then for Lebesgue-a.e. u ∈ ℝ^k the following holds: if F(u) ∈ Y, F is differentiable at u and DF(u) is injective, then Y has approximate tangent space DF(u)(ℝ^k) at F(u). That is, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt k Y (F u) (LinearMap.range (fderiv ℝ F u)) in the sense of SimonGMT (Simon Ch. 3, 1.4).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ) (F : Euclid k → Euclid P) (Y : Set (Euclid P)) (K : NNReal), 0 < k → LipschitzWith K F → MeasurableSet Y → (∀ C : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact C → μHE[k] (Y ∩ C) ≠ ∞) → ∀ᵐ u ∂(volume : Measure (Euclid k)), F u ∈ Y → DifferentiableAt ℝ F u → Function.Injective (fderiv ℝ F u) → HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt k Y (F u) (LinearMap.range (fderiv ℝ F u : Euclid k →ₗ[ℝ] Euclid P))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Notation and tools.
- For a linear D : ℝ^k → ℝ^P let J(D) := det(D*D)^{1/2}, and JF(u) := J(DF(u)) where F is differentiable. G_F := {u : F differentiable at u, DF(u) injective}; G_F is Borel and JF is Borel (Mathlib measurable_fderiv).
- c_A := min_{|w|=1}|Aw| for injective linear A.
- η_{y,r}(z) := r⁻¹(z − y) (SimonGMT blowUpMap). For every set A, H^k(η_{y,r}(A)) = r^{−k}H^k(A) (Mathlib euclideanHausdorffMeasure_homothety_image and translation invariance).
- Area formula. For F Lipschitz and injective on a Borel B, and Borel g ≥ 0, ∫_{F(B)} g dH^k = ∫_B g(F(u))JF(u) du (SimonGMT weighted_area_formula_lipschitz_injOn, in Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.AreaLipschitz).
 This is the only fact used here that lies outside the contract import closure, and it is used only in step 7. This child has no dependencies and machine leaves cannot add imports. So it must be decomposed so that the area-formula step lies in its own assembly proof, and that proof adds `import Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.AreaLipschitz` to GMT/Ch07/Submission.lean. Precedent: the accepted parent dtc_isIntegerMultiplicity_sub added a SimonGMT import, and imports propagate to dependents through the dependency merge.
- Linear area formula. For injective linear D : ℝ^k → ℝ^P, ∫_{D(ℝ^k)} φ dH^k = J(D)∫_{ℝ^k} φ(Dw) dw. This is in scope: write D = ι∘A with ι : ℝ^k → D(ℝ^k) a linear isometry and A invertible with |det A| = J(D); use isometry invariance of μHE[k], EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume and Mathlib Measure.addHaar_image_linearMap.
- Lipschitz image bound. H^k(G(A)) ≤ Lip(G)^k H^k(A) for G Lipschitz on A (SimonGMT euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_le_of_lipschitzOn, in scope via Chapter02.Lipschitz); on ℝ^k, H^k = L^k.
- All other facts used are in scope after `import GMT.Ch07.Submission`: Mathlib exists_partition_approximatesLinearOn_of_hasFDerivWithinAt, MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn (Lusin–Souslin), Besicovitch.ae_tendsto_measure_inter_div, Besicovitch.ae_tendsto_rnDeriv, VitaliFamily.ae_tendsto_average_norm_sub, LipschitzWith.ae_differentiableAt, and EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume.
1. (Bi-Lipschitz pieces.)
 - Apply exists_partition_approximatesLinearOn_of_hasFDerivWithinAt to F on the Borel set G_F with derivative fderiv ℝ F, taking r(A) := c_A/2 if A is injective and r(A) := 1 otherwise; r(A) > 0 for every A.
 - This gives countably many pairwise disjoint Borel sets t_i covering G_F and linear maps A_i such that |F(v) − F(w) − A_i(v − w)| ≤ r(A_i)|v − w| for v, w ∈ G_F ∩ t_i. If G_F ∩ t_i ≠ ∅, then A_i = DF(y_i) for some y_i ∈ G_F, so A_i is injective.
 - Put T_i := G_F ∩ t_i. For v, w ∈ T_i, |F(v) − F(w)| ≥ |A_i(v − w)| − (c_{A_i}/2)|v − w| ≥ (c_{A_i}/2)|v − w|.
 Since the exceptional set of the claim is a countable union over i, it suffices to prove the claim for a.e. u ∈ T := T_i, where F is bi-Lipschitz with lower constant c > 0.
2. (The image of a piece.) Let T' := T ∩ F⁻¹(Y) (Borel) and N := F(T').
 - N is Borel by Lusin–Souslin, F being continuous and injective on T'. Also N ⊆ Y.
 - The inverse ψ := (F|_{T'})⁻¹ : N → T' is c⁻¹-Lipschitz.
 - For every ball, H^k(N ∩ B_r(y)) ≤ K^k L^k(T' ∩ F⁻¹B_r(y)) ≤ K^k ω_k (r/c)^k, with ω_k := L^k(B_1). This uses the Lipschitz image bound H^k(F(A)) ≤ K^k L^k(A) and T' ∩ F⁻¹B_r(y) ⊆ B_{r/c}(ψ(y)) for y ∈ N.
 - N is locally H^k-finite.
3. (Null sets pull back.) If Z ⊆ N is H^k-null, then T' ∩ F⁻¹(Z) = ψ(Z) is L^k-null, by the Lipschitz image bound for the c⁻¹-Lipschitz map ψ and H^k = L^k on ℝ^k.
4. (Y ∖ N has density zero at a.e. point of N.)
 - The locally finite Borel measures ν := H^k⌞(Y ∖ N) and λ := H^k⌞N are mutually singular: they are concentrated on the disjoint sets Y ∖ N and N.
 - By Besicovitch differentiation (Besicovitch.ae_tendsto_rnDeriv for ν with respect to λ, whose Radon–Nikodym derivative is 0), ν(B̄_r(y))/λ(B̄_r(y)) → 0 for λ-a.e. y.
 - By step 2, λ(B̄_r(y)) ≤ K^k ω_k ((r + ε)/c)^k ≤ C r^k for small r and every ε ∈ (0, r). Hence r^{−k}H^k((Y ∖ N) ∩ B̄_r(y)) → 0 for H^k-a.e. y ∈ N.
 - Let Z_bad ⊆ N be the H^k-null exceptional set. By step 3, T' ∩ F⁻¹(Z_bad) is L^k-null.
 - Consequence. Let y ∈ N ∖ Z_bad and φ ∈ C_c(ℝ^P) with spt φ ⊆ B_{R₀}(0). Since N ⊆ Y,
 |∫_{η_{y,r}(Y)} φ dH^k − ∫_{η_{y,r}(N)} φ dH^k| ≤ ‖φ‖_∞ H^k(η_{y,r}(Y ∖ N) ∩ B_{R₀}(0)) = ‖φ‖_∞ r^{−k} H^k((Y ∖ N) ∩ B̄_{rR₀}(y)) → 0.
 Both integrals are finite, since φ is bounded with compact support and Y, N are locally finite.
5. (Good points.) Call u ∈ T' good if:
 - u ∉ F⁻¹(Z_bad);
 - u is a Lebesgue density point of T', i.e. L^k(B_ρ(u) ∖ T')/L^k(B_ρ(u)) → 0 (Besicovitch.ae_tendsto_measure_inter_div);
 - u is a Lebesgue point of the bounded Borel function 1_{T'}·JF, i.e. ρ^{−k}∫_{B_ρ(u)}|1_{T'}JF − JF(u)| → 0 (VitaliFamily.ae_tendsto_average_norm_sub for the Besicovitch Vitali family; 0 ≤ JF ≤ K^k).
 L^k-a.e. u ∈ T' is good (step 4 and Lebesgue differentiation). Fix a good u and put y := F(u) and D := DF(u).
6. (Lower bound |Dw| ≥ c|w|.) Let w ≠ 0 and ε ∈ (0, 1).
 - For small ρ > 0 the ball B_{ερ|w|}(u + ρw) meets T'. Otherwise B_{2ρ|w|}(u) ∖ T' contains it, a fixed fraction (ε/2)^k of L^k(B_{2ρ|w|}(u)), for arbitrarily small ρ, contradicting density. Pick v_ρ ∈ T' in that ball.
 - Then c|v_ρ − u| ≤ |F(v_ρ) − F(u)| = |D(v_ρ − u)| + o(ρ) ≤ ρ|Dw| + ‖D‖ερ|w| + o(ρ), and |v_ρ − u| ≥ (1 − ε)ρ|w|.
 - Divide by ρ, let ρ ↓ 0, then ε ↓ 0: |Dw| ≥ c|w|.
7. (Blow-up of N.) Let φ ∈ C_c(ℝ^P) with spt φ ⊆ B_{R₀}(0). Put Φ_r(w) := (F(u + rw) − F(u))/r. By the scaling identity, the area formula on T' (F injective there) and the substitution v = u + rw,
 ∫_{η_{y,r}(N)} φ dH^k = r^{−k}∫_{T'} φ((F(v) − y)/r) JF(v) dv = ∫ 1_{T'}(u + rw) JF(u + rw) φ(Φ_r(w)) dw.
 - Cutoff. For u + rw ∈ T', |Φ_r(w)| ≥ c|w|, so the integrand vanishes unless |w| < R₁ := R₀/c.
 - Convergence. As r ↓ 0, Φ_r → D uniformly on B̄_{R₁}(0) (Fréchet differentiability), hence φ∘Φ_r → φ∘D uniformly there (uniform continuity of φ). Also ∫_{B_{R₁}}|1_{T'}(u + rw)JF(u + rw) − JF(u)| dw = r^{−k}∫_{B_{rR₁}(u)}|1_{T'}JF − JF(u)| → 0 (good point).
 - Limit. Hence ∫_{η_{y,r}(N)} φ dH^k → JF(u)∫_{B_{R₁}} φ(Dw) dw = J(D)∫_{ℝ^k} φ(Dw) dw = ∫_{D(ℝ^k)} φ dH^k. The middle step holds because φ(Dw) = 0 for |w| ≥ R₁ by step 6; the last is the linear area formula.
8. (Conclusion.) By steps 4 and 7, ∫_{η_{y,r}(Y)} φ dH^k → ∫_{D(ℝ^k)} φ dH^k as r ↓ 0, for every φ ∈ C_c(ℝ^P). Since D is injective, finrank D(ℝ^k) = k. Hence HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt k Y (F u) (range DF(u)) for every good u ∈ T'. The exceptional u in T ∩ F⁻¹(Y) form an L^k-null set; with step 1, this proves the claim. ∎
proof_key_steps: Mathlib's approximatesLinearOn partition splits the regular set of F into countably many pieces on which F is bi-Lipschitz.
On a piece, N = F(T ∩ F⁻¹Y) ⊆ Y has H^k(N ∩ B_r) ≤ Cr^k; Besicovitch differentiation of the mutually singular H^k⌞(Y∖N) against H^k⌞N shows Y ∖ N has density zero at a.e. point of N.

At Lebesgue density points of the piece that are Lebesgue points of 1_T JF, the area formula rewrites the blow-ups of N as integrals over rescaled parameters that converge to J(DF)∫φ(DF w)dw = ∫_{DF(ℝ^k)} φ dH^k.
Density zero of Y ∖ N transfers the limit from N to Y.

subproblem.title: Cone filling inside a subspace: an integer multiplicity cycle with compact support in a linear subspace V bounds an integer multiplicity current with compact support in V
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (X : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) m) (V : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)), 0 < m → IsIntegerMultiplicity X → BoundaryVanishes X → IsCompact X.support → X.support ⊆ (V : Set (Euclid P)) → ∃ Y : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (m + 1), IsIntegerMultiplicity Y ∧ Y.boundary = X ∧ IsCompact Y.support ∧ Y.support ⊆ (V : Set (Euclid P))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Notation and conventions.
- k := m ≥ 1. A test p-form is a C^∞ compactly supported map ℝ^P → Λ^p = Covector (Euclid P) p.
- H^p := μHE[p], equal to Lebesgue measure on p-dimensional subspaces.
- For a linear D : ℝ^p → ℝ^P, J(D) := det(D*D)^{1/2}, and ∂F(u) := (DF(u)e_1, …, DF(u)e_p). G_F := {u : F differentiable at u, DF(u) injective}.
- For injective D, ξ_D(α) := α(De_1, …, De_p)/J(D). By Gram–Schmidt (De = Rτ with R upper triangular, det R = J(D)), this equals α(τ) for an orthonormal basis τ of D(ℝ^p). So ξ_D is a unit orientation of D(ℝ^p) in the sense of IsUnitOrientationOf.
- Two unit orientations of the same plane differ by a sign, because orthonormal bases differ by an orthogonal matrix of determinant ±1.
Sibling children used:
- lipschitz_tangent (tangent identification along Lipschitz maps);
- the accepted imrep_carrier_sdiff_support_null (reuse sibling carrier_sdiff): if R represents T in an open U, then H^p(R.carrier ∖ spt T) = 0.
Imports. Steps 7–9 use the SimonGMT area formula weighted_area_formula_lipschitz_injOn and area_image_compl_regularSet_eq_zero, in Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.AreaLipschitz, outside the contract import closure. The Lipschitz image bound euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_le_of_lipschitzOn is in scope via Chapter02.Lipschitz. The node that formalizes those steps needs `import Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.AreaLipschitz`. It is inherited through the dependency merge from the sibling lipschitz_tangent, which must add it. Otherwise add it in an assembly (non-leaf) proof, since machine leaves cannot add imports; precedent: the accepted parent dtc_isIntegerMultiplicity_sub. All other cited facts (Mathlib) are in scope.
0. (Support vanishing for X.) Let X = τ(M, θ, ξ) be an IMRep of X. By carrier_sdiff, H^k(M ∖ spt X) = 0. Hence, if a test k-form γ vanishes at every point of spt X — in particular if tsupport γ ∩ spt X = ∅ — then X(γ) = ∫_M θξ(γ) dH^k = 0. If spt X = ∅, then X = 0 and Y := 0 works (∂0 = 0, spt 0 = ∅). Assume spt X ≠ ∅.
1. (Homotopy operator.) For p ≥ 1 and a C^∞ p-form β, define the (p−1)-form
 (K_pβ)(x) := ∫_0^1 t^{p−1} ι_x(β(tx)) dt, where ι_x α := ContinuousAlternatingMap.curryLeft α x.
 - This is a Bochner integral in the finite-dimensional Λ^{p−1}, with integrand C^∞ in (t, x).
 - K_pβ is C^∞, and its x-derivatives are obtained by differentiating under the integral sign.
 - If β(tx) = 0 for all t ∈ [0, 1], then (K_pβ)(x) = 0.
2. (Homotopy formula: β = d(K_pβ) + K_{p+1}(dβ) for p ≥ 1.) Fix x and v_1, …, v_p, and use dγ(x)(w_0, …, w_q) = Σ_i (−1)^i Dγ(x)[w_i](…ŵ_i…) (SimonGMT exteriorDerivative_apply).
 - d(K_pβ)(x)(v) = ∫_0^1 [p t^{p−1}β(tx)(v) + t^p Σ_i (−1)^{i−1} Dβ(tx)[v_i](x, v_1, …, v̂_i, …, v_p)] dt.
 - K_{p+1}(dβ)(x)(v) = ∫_0^1 t^p [Dβ(tx)[x](v) + Σ_i (−1)^i Dβ(tx)[v_i](x, v_1, …, v̂_i, …, v_p)] dt.
 - Adding, the sums cancel, leaving ∫_0^1 (d/dt)(t^p β(tx)(v)) dt = β(x)(v), since p ≥ 1.
3. (Definition of Y.) spt X is compact. Choose δ > 0 and ζ ∈ C_c^∞(ℝ^P) with 0 ≤ ζ ≤ 1 and ζ = 1 on the open set N_δ := thickening δ (spt X) (Mathlib exists_contDiff_support_eq_eq_one_iff applied to cthickening δ (spt X) ⊆ thickening 2δ (spt X)). For a test (k+1)-form ω, ζK_{k+1}ω is a test k-form with tsupport in tsupport ζ. Define Y(ω) := X(ζK_{k+1}ω); Y is linear.
4. (Y is a current.) Let ω_j → 0 in the test-form topology, with supports in a compact K₁ and all derivatives tending to 0 uniformly.
 - Then ε_{j,a} := sup_y ‖D^aω_j(y)‖ → 0 for every a, since ω_j vanishes off K₁.
 - (K_{k+1}ω_j)(x) = ∫_0^1 t^k Π(ω_j(tx), x) dt, with Π(α, x) := ι_xα bounded bilinear. The Leibniz rule gives ‖D^a(K_{k+1}ω_j)(x)‖ ≤ C_a(1 + |x|) max_{b≤a} ε_{j,b}.
 - Hence ζK_{k+1}ω_j → 0 in the test-form topology, with supports in tsupport ζ, and Y(ω_j) → 0 by continuity of X.
 So Y ∈ 𝒟_{k+1}(ℝ^P).
5. (∂Y = X.) Let ω be a test k-form. Then ∂Y(ω) = Y(dω) = X(ζK_{k+1}dω). Step 2 with p = k ≥ 1 gives K_{k+1}dω = ω − d(K_kω), so ∂Y(ω) = X(ζω) − X(ζ d(K_kω)).
 - First term: ζω − ω vanishes on N_δ ⊇ spt X, so X(ζω) = X(ω) by step 0.
 - Second term: ζK_kω is a test (k−1)-form. The k-forms ζ d(K_kω) and d(ζK_kω) agree on N_δ, where ζ ≡ 1 near every point and d is local; their difference vanishes on spt X. So X(ζ d(K_kω)) = X(d(ζK_kω)) = (∂X)(ζK_kω) = 0 by step 0, because ∂X = 0 (k ≥ 1).
 Hence ∂Y(ω) = X(ω), i.e. Y.boundary = X.
6. (Support.) C₀ := {sx : s ∈ [0, 1], x ∈ spt X} is compact, as the continuous image of [0, 1] × spt X. Moreover C₀ ⊆ V, since spt X ⊆ V and V is a linear subspace.
 - Let ω be a test (k+1)-form with tsupport ω ∩ C₀ = ∅. The set W := {x : sx ∉ tsupport ω for all s ∈ [0, 1]} is open, because [0, 1] is compact so the projection is a closed map. W ⊇ spt X.
 - (K_{k+1}ω)(x) = 0 for x ∈ W (step 1), so ζK_{k+1}ω vanishes on spt X, and Y(ω) = 0 by step 0.
 - For x ∉ C₀ choose r > 0 with B̄_{2r}(x) ∩ C₀ = ∅. The ball B_r(x) is open with compact closure, and Y vanishes on every test form supported in it. So B_r(x) lies in the zero region of Y and x ∉ spt Y.
 Thus spt Y ⊆ C₀ ⊆ V, and spt Y is compact (closed in the compact C₀).
7. (Integral Lipschitz parametrization of X.) Claim: there are Lipschitz F_j : ℝ^k → ℝ^P, Borel A_j ⊆ G_{F_j} with F_j(A_j) ⊆ spt X, and measurable g_j : ℝ^k → ℤ (j ∈ ℕ) such that:
 (LF) Σ_j ∫_{A_j ∩ F_j⁻¹(C)} |g_j| JF_j < ∞ for every compact C;
 (REP) X(γ) = Σ_j ∫_{A_j} g_j(u) γ(F_j(u))(∂F_j(u)) du for every test k-form γ.
 Construction:
 (a) By step 0, H^k(M ∖ spt X) = 0, and spt X is closed.
 (b) Pieces. By countable rectifiability, M ⊆ M_null ∪ ⋃_i F̃_i(ℝ^k) with H^k(M_null) = 0 and F̃_i Lipschitz. The Borel sets E_i := {u ∈ G_{F̃_i} : F̃_i(u) ∈ M ∩ spt X} are split by Mathlib exists_partition_approximatesLinearOn_of_hasFDerivWithinAt into Borel pieces.
 - The tolerance is r(A) := c_A/2 for injective A and r(A) := 1 otherwise, where c_A := min_{|w|=1}|Aw|. The approximating maps are A = DF̃_i(y) for points y of E_i, so they are injective, and F̃_i is bi-Lipschitz on each piece.
 - Enumerate the pieces as (Φ_l, P_l), and disjointify the images: P'_l := P_l ∖ Φ_l⁻¹(⋃_{l'<l} Φ_{l'}(P_{l'})). Images of Borel sets under maps that are continuous and injective on them are Borel (Lusin–Souslin, MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn).

subproblem.title: Coarea formula along a spine: slicing a rectifiable set whose approximate tangent planes contain L by the orthogonal projection onto L
subproblem.statement:
Setting:
- P, n ∈ ℕ and L ⊆ ℝ^P a linear subspace with d := dim L < n; put m := n − d ≥ 1.
- p := L.starProjection is the orthogonal projection onto L, viewed as a map ℝ^P → ℝ^P, and H^k := μHE[k].
- For t ∈ L, M_t := M ∩ p⁻¹(t) = M ∩ {x : L.starProjection x = t}.
Hypotheses on M ⊆ ℝ^P:
- M is Borel and countably n-rectifiable;
- H^n(M ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K;
- for H^n-a.e. x ∈ M there is a subspace Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q and L ⊆ Q.
Conclusions:
(i) For H^d-a.e. t ∈ L (i.e. μHE[d]⌞L-a.e.), M_t is countably m-rectifiable. Moreover, for H^m-a.e. x ∈ M_t and every subspace Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q, we have HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt m M_t x (Q ∩ L^⊥).
(ii) For every Borel g : ℝ^P → [0, ∞], the function t ↦ ∫_{M_t} g dH^m is a.e.-measurable for H^d⌞L, and
 ∫_M g dH^n = ∫_L (∫_{M_t} g dH^m) dH^d(t).
This is Federer 3.2.22 for the map p restricted to M. Its coarea factor is 1, because on T_xM ⊇ L the map p is the orthogonal projection onto L.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Notation and tools.
- q := I − p = Lᗮ.starProjection, so x = p(x) + q(x) with p(x) ∈ L and q(x) ∈ L^⊥.
- On a k-dimensional subspace, H^k is k-dimensional Lebesgue measure. This follows from isometry invariance of μHE and EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume.
- Jacobians. For a linear D : ℝ^k → ℝ^P, J(D) := det(D*D)^{1/2}. For a Lipschitz F : ℝ^k → ℝ^P, JF(u) := J(DF(u)) where F is differentiable (Rademacher: a.e.).
- G_F := {u : F differentiable at u, DF(u) injective}.
Facts used:
(T1) Area formula and Lipschitz images.
 - (T1a) Area formula: for F : ℝ^k → ℝ^P Lipschitz and injective on a Borel set B, and Borel g ≥ 0, ∫_{F(B)} g dH^k = ∫_B g(F(u)) JF(u) du (SimonGMT weighted_area_formula_lipschitz_injOn).
 - (T1b) Sard-type statement: H^k(F(ℝ^k ∖ G_F)) = 0 (SimonGMT area_image_compl_regularSet_eq_zero).
 - (T1c) Lipschitz image bound: H^k(F(Z)) ≤ Lip(F)^k L^k(Z) for every Z (SimonGMT euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_le_of_lipschitzOn).
 Imports. (T1a) and (T1b) are in Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.AreaLipschitz, outside the contract import closure; they are used in steps 1 and 5. (T1c) is in scope via Chapter02.Lipschitz. The node that formalizes steps 1 and 5 must have `import Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.AreaLipschitz` in GMT/Ch07/Submission.lean. It is inherited through the dependency merge if the sibling lipschitz_tangent added it (it must, for its own area-formula step); otherwise add it in an assembly (non-leaf) proof, since machine leaves cannot add imports. Precedent: the accepted parent dtc_isIntegerMultiplicity_sub added a SimonGMT import.
 All other facts cited below are in scope after `import GMT.Ch07.Submission`.
(T2) Bi-Lipschitz pieces (Mathlib exists_partition_approximatesLinearOn_of_hasFDerivWithinAt). Let G ⊆ ℝ^k be Borel with F differentiable at every point of G, and let r be a function on linear maps with r(A) > 0 for every A; we use r(A) := c_A/16 if A is injective and r(A) := 1 otherwise, where c_A := min_{|w|=1}|Aw|. Then G ⊆ ⋃_i t_i for pairwise disjoint Borel sets t_i, with linear maps A_i such that:
 - |F(v) − F(w) − A_i(v − w)| ≤ r(A_i)|v − w| for v, w ∈ G ∩ t_i;
 - if G ∩ t_i ≠ ∅, then A_i = DF(y_i) for some y_i ∈ G (not necessarily in t_i).
(T3) Tangent planes along Lipschitz maps: the sibling child lipschitz_tangent. Let k ≥ 1, F : ℝ^k → ℝ^P Lipschitz, and Y ⊆ ℝ^P Borel and locally H^k-finite. Then for L^k-a.e. u with F(u) ∈ Y and u ∈ G_F, Y has approximate tangent space DF(u)(ℝ^k) at F(u).
(T5) Fubini. A linear isometry ℝ^d × ℝ^m ≅ L × K (orthonormal coordinates) carries product Lebesgue measure to H^d⌞L ⊗ H^m⌞K. Use Mathlib Submodule.measurePreserving_measurableEquivProd and Tonelli (lintegral_prod).

(T4) Eilenberg inequality for p. If Z ⊆ ℝ^P and H^n(Z) = 0, then H^m(Z ∩ p⁻¹(t)) = 0 for H^d-a.e. t ∈ L.
Proof: H^n(Z) = 0 means μH[n](Z) = 0. So for each j there is a countable cover (C_i^j)_i of Z with diam C_i^j < 1/j and Σ_i (diam C_i^j)^n < 4^{−j}. Put
 φ_j(t) := Σ_i 1_{p(cl C_i^j)}(t)(diam C_i^j)^m.
 This is Borel: p(cl C) is compact for bounded C. Since p is 1-Lipschitz, p(cl C_i^j) lies in a ball of L of radius diam C_i^j, so H^d(p(cl C_i^j)) ≤ ω_d (diam C_i^j)^d. Therefore
 ∫_L φ_j dH^d ≤ ω_d Σ_i (diam C_i^j)^n < ω_d 4^{−j}.
 By Markov's inequality and Borel–Cantelli, φ_j(t) → 0 for H^d-a.e. t ∈ L. For such t, the sets C_i^j with t ∈ p(C_i^j) cover Z ∩ p⁻¹(t). Hence the 1/j-premeasure satisfies μH[m]_{1/j}(Z ∩ p⁻¹(t)) ≤ φ_j(t) → 0. These premeasures increase to μH[m](Z ∩ p⁻¹(t)) as j → ∞, so that value is 0. ∎(T4)

Main proof.
1. (Parametrization.) By countable rectifiability, M ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_j F_j(ℝ^n) with H^n(M₀) = 0 and F_j : ℝ^n → ℝ^P Lipschitz. By (T1b), H^n(F_j(ℝ^n ∖ G_{F_j})) = 0.
2. (Good parameters.)
 - Bad points of M. Let Bad ⊆ M be the H^n-null set of x ∈ M at which no approximate tangent space Q ⊇ L exists, and let Bad' ⊇ Bad be Borel and H^n-null.
 - The sets E_j. Put E_j := G_{F_j} ∩ F_j⁻¹(M ∖ Bad'), a Borel set. By (T3) applied to (F_j, Y := M), there is a Borel L^n-null set N_j such that for u ∈ E_j ∖ N_j, M has approximate tangent space DF_j(u)(ℝ^n) at F_j(u). This space contains L, by uniqueness of approximate tangent spaces (SimonGMT HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique) and F_j(u) ∉ Bad.
 - The sets U'_j. Put U'_j := E_j ∖ N_j (Borel). By (T1c), H^n(F_j(N_j)) = 0. Hence M ∖ ⋃_j F_j(U'_j) ⊆ M₀ ∪ Bad' ∪ ⋃_j [F_j(ℝ^n ∖ G_{F_j}) ∪ F_j(N_j)] is H^n-null.
 Apply (T2) to F_j on G := U'_j. This gives countably many Borel pieces T := U'_j ∩ t_i, with F := F_j and A = A_T = DF(u_T) for some u_T ∈ U'_j, such that:
 (a) |F(v) − F(w) − A(v − w)| ≤ (c_A/16)|v − w| on T, hence |F(v) − F(w)| ≥ (15c_A/16)|v − w| on T;
 (b) every u ∈ T is good: F(u) ∈ M, DF(u) is injective, and T_{F(u)}M = DF(u)(ℝ^n) ⊇ L;
 (c) A is injective and L ⊆ A(ℝ^n), because u_T ∈ U'_j is good.
 The union of the images F(T) over all pieces covers M up to an H^n-null set.
3. (Adapted coordinates on a piece.)
 - Surjectivity of p∘A. Let ℓ ∈ L. By (c) there is w with Aw = ℓ and |w| ≤ |ℓ|/c_A, and then p(Aw) = ℓ. So p∘A : ℝ^n → L is onto.
 - Splitting. K := ker(p∘A) has dimension m. On K' := K^⊥ we have |pAa| ≥ c_A|a|, since the minimal-norm preimage lies in K'.
 - The map Φ. Define Φ : ℝ^n → L × K by Φ(u) := (pF(u), π_K u).
 - Φ is bi-Lipschitz on T. For v, w ∈ T write v − w = a + b with a ∈ K' and b ∈ K. Then pF(v) − pF(w) = pAa + p(e) with |e| ≤ (c_A/16)(|a| + |b|).
  - If |b| ≥ |a|: |Φ(v) − Φ(w)| ≥ |b| ≥ |v − w|/√2.
  - If |b| < |a|: |pF(v) − pF(w)| ≥ c_A|a| − (c_A/8)|a| ≥ (7c_A/8)|v − w|/√2.
  So |Φ(v) − Φ(w)| ≥ κ|v − w| on T, with κ := min(1, 7c_A/8)/√2 > 0.
 - The parametrization H. Ω := Φ(T) is Borel (Lusin–Souslin). H := F∘(Φ|_T)⁻¹ : Ω → ℝ^P is Lipschitz and injective, with Lipschitz inverse Φ∘(F|_T)⁻¹ on F(T). Extend H to a Lipschitz map L × K → ℝ^P coordinatewise (McShane: LipschitzOnWith.extend_real applied to each coordinate of an orthonormal basis of ℝ^P).
 - p(H(t, b)) = t for (t, b) ∈ Ω.
 - Identify L × K with ℝ^n through orthonormal coordinates as in (T5).
4. (Jacobian identity.) Fix (t, b) ∈ Ω such that:
 - (t, b) is a density point of Ω;
 - H is differentiable at (t, b);
 - with x := H(t, b), DH(t, b) is injective and M has approximate tangent space DH(t, b)(ℝ^n) at x.
 These hold at L^n-a.e. (t, b) ∈ Ω: Rademacher; the lower Lipschitz bound |H(z) − H(z')| ≥ κ'|z − z'| on Ω (κ' > 0, step 3) passes to DH at Lebesgue density points z of Ω where H is differentiable. Given |w| = 1 and ε ∈ (0, 1), for small ρ the ball B_{ερ}(z + ρw) meets Ω, since otherwise a fixed fraction of B_{2ρ}(z) misses Ω. A point z_ρ there gives κ'(1 − ε)ρ ≤ |H(z_ρ) − H(z)| ≤ ρ|DH(z)w| + ‖DH(z)‖ερ + o(ρ), so |DH(z)w| ≥ κ' after letting ρ ↓ 0 and then ε ↓ 0. Finally, (T3) applies to (H, M).
 By uniqueness and step 2(b), R := DH(t, b)(ℝ^n) = T_xM ⊇ L.
 - Differentiating p∘H(t', b') = t' along Ω at a density point gives p∘∂_tH = id_L and p∘∂_bH = 0, where DH = [∂_tH | ∂_bH] with ∂_tH : L → ℝ^P and ∂_bH : K → ℝ^P.
 - Hence ∂_bH(K) ⊆ R ∩ L^⊥. Since L ⊆ R, we have R = L ⊕ (R ∩ L^⊥) and dim(R ∩ L^⊥) = m. ∂_bH is injective, so ∂_bH(K) = R ∩ L^⊥.
 - For ℓ ∈ L, ∂_tH(ℓ) − ℓ = q∂_tH(ℓ) ∈ R ∩ L^⊥. So ∂_tH(ℓ) = ℓ + ∂_bH(Bℓ) for a linear B : L → K.
 - Thus DH(t, b) = D₀∘U, with D₀(ℓ, κ) := ℓ + ∂_bH(κ) and U(ℓ, κ) := (ℓ, κ + Bℓ). U is unipotent, so det U = 1.
 - D₀ maps L isometrically into L and K into L^⊥ ⊥ L. So D₀*D₀ = diag(I_L, (∂_bH)*∂_bH).
 - Hence J(DH(t, b)) = J(D₀)|det U| = J(∂_bH(t, b)) =: J_bH(t, b), and ∂_bH(t, b)(K) = T_xM ∩ L^⊥.
5. (Coarea on one piece.) Let g ≥ 0 be Borel. By (T1a) for H on Ω and step 4,
 ∫_{F(T)} g dH^n = ∫_Ω g(H) JH = ∫_Ω g(H) J_bH.

 For each t, H_t := H(t, ·) : K → ℝ^P is Lipschitz and injective on Ω_t, and H_t(Ω_t) = F(T) ∩ p⁻¹(t). Indeed every x ∈ F(T) with p(x) = t is H(t, π_K(F|_T)⁻¹x).
 By Tonelli applied to the null set of bad (t, b), for H^d-a.e. t the following holds for L^m-a.e. b ∈ Ω_t: H_t is differentiable at b with DH_t(b) = ∂_bH(t, b).
 Hence, for a.e. t, (T1a) for H_t gives ∫_{F(T) ∩ p⁻¹(t)} g dH^m = ∫_{Ω_t} g(H(t, b)) J_bH(t, b) db.
 Therefore ∫_{F(T)} g dH^n = ∫_L ∫_{F(T)∩p⁻¹(t)} g dH^m dt, with an a.e.-measurable inner function.
6. (Summation; proof of (ii).)
 - Disjoint pieces. Enumerate the pieces as (T_l, F_l, H_l, Ω_l)_{l∈ℕ}. Put P'_l := F_l(T_l) ∖ ⋃_{l'<l} F_{l'}(T_{l'}). These sets are Borel and pairwise disjoint, their union is N_M := ⋃_l F_l(T_l) ⊆ M, and Z := M ∖ N_M is Borel with H^n(Z) = 0 (step 2).
 - Applying step 5 to g·1_{P'_l} and summing by monotone convergence gives ∫_{N_M} g dH^n = ∫_L ∫_{N_M ∩ p⁻¹(t)} g dH^m dt.
 - By (T4), H^m(Z ∩ p⁻¹(t)) = 0 for a.e. t, so ∫_{M_t} g dH^m = ∫_{N_M ∩ p⁻¹(t)} g dH^m for a.e. t.
 - Also ∫_M g dH^n = ∫_{N_M} g dH^n, which proves (ii). The a.e.-measurability holds because a countable sum of a.e.-measurable functions is a.e.-measurable.

8. (Tangent planes of slices; proof of (i).)
 - Local finiteness. By (ii) with g = 1_{B̄_j}, ∫_L H^m(M_t ∩ B̄_j) dt = H^n(M ∩ B̄_j) < ∞. So for a.e. t, M_t is locally H^m-finite (countably many j).
 - Fix l. For a.e. t, apply (T3) to the Lipschitz map H_l(t, ·) and Y := M_t (Borel, locally finite). For L^m-a.e. b ∈ (Ω_l)_t such that (t, b) is good in step 4, M_t has approximate tangent space ∂_bH_l(t, b)(K_l) = T_xM ∩ L^⊥ at x = H_l(t, b). Here DH_l(t, ·)(b) = ∂_bH_l(t, b) is injective.
 - The bad (t, b) form a null set, so for a.e. t only an L^m-null set of b is bad. By (T1c), H_l(t, ·) maps these null sets to H^m-null sets.

 - If Q is any subspace with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q, then Q = T_xM by uniqueness. So HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt m M_t x (Q ∩ L^⊥), and finrank(Q ∩ L^⊥) = n − d = m because L ⊆ Q. This proves (i). ∎

Notation.
- p := L.starProjection and q := Lᗮ.starProjection; t^a(x) := ⟨f_a, x⟩, so p(x) = Σ_a t^a(x)f_a.
- H^j := μHE[j]; on j-dimensional subspaces it is Lebesgue measure (isometry invariance and EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume), so in the coordinates t^a, H^d⌞L is Lebesgue measure on ℝ^d.
- M_W(T) := T.massOn W and M(T) := M_{ℝ^P}(T). For an IM current T, μ_T is the measure of a representation; it is independent of the representation by (F3).
- Translates: (τ_vT)(ω) := T(ω(· + v)) = currentEval (blowUp T (−v) 1) ω. Translating an IMRep by v (carrier + v, mult and orient composed with · − v) gives an IMRep of τ_vT with the translated measure; approximate tangent spaces translate. Mass is translation invariant.
- Sums of currents are written A + B := A − (0 − B), since GeometricCurrentOn has only Sub and Zero. Mass is subadditive, M_W(A + B) ≤ M_W(A) + M_W(B), directly from the sup definition of massOn.
Sibling children used:
- cone_filling_subspace;
- the accepted declarations (reuse siblings):
 (F1) imrep_represents_massOn_eq_measure: M_W(T) = μ_T(W) for open W;
 (F3) imrep_measure_eq_of_represents_same_current;
 (F4) rsd_isIntegerMultiplicity_int_combination: if T₁, T₂ are IM and T(ω) = p₁T₁(ω) + p₂T₂(ω) for all ω (p_i ∈ ℤ), then T is IM;

 (F7) dtc_imrep_current: every IMRep represents some current.
 Facts for an IM current T with representation R = (M_T, θ_T, ξ_T):
 (a) T(γ) = ∫_{M_T} θ_Tξ_T(γ) dH = 0 if γ vanishes on spt T, by (F6);
 (b) μ_T(ℝ^P ∖ spt T) = ∫_{M_T ∖ spt T} θ_T dH = 0, by (F6);
 (c) if μ_T(O) = 0 for an open set O, then T vanishes on test forms supported in O, because the integrand is supported in M_T ∩ O, a null set. Every point of O has a ball with compact closure inside O, so spt T ∩ O = ∅. This is immediate from the representation.

PART I. Tools.
I.1 (Interior product with an orthonormal frame.) Let g = (g_1, …, g_k) be orthonormal and k + m' = n' (formalize with an explicit m' and h : n' = k + m', to avoid degree casts).
 - For α ∈ Λ^{n'} define ♭_gα(v) := α(Fin.append g v ∘ Fin.cast h), i.e. α(g_1, …, g_k, v_1, …, v_{m'}).
 - Updating one entry of v updates one entry of Fin.append g v (Fin.addCases). Hence ♭_gα is multilinear, and alternating because equal entries stay at distinct indices; and |♭_gα(v)| ≤ ‖α‖∏|v_j|.
 - So ♭_g : Λ^{n'} →L[ℝ] Λ^{m'} is continuous linear with ‖♭_g‖ ≤ 1 (LinearMap.mkContinuous).
 - For a test n'-form ω, ♭_gω(t + ·) := y ↦ ♭_g(ω(t + y)) is a test m'-form with tsupport ⊆ tsupport ω − t.
 - For g = f, k = d and m' = m, any ♭ as in the hypothesis equals ♭_f, both being given by the same formula. So the product formula reads S(ω) = ∫_L S₀(♭_fω(t + ·)) dt.
I.2 (Tangent planes inside a subspace.) If H^j(M' ∖ V) = 0 for a linear subspace V, y ∈ V and HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt j M' y Q, then Q ⊆ V.
 Proof:
 - Suppose z ∈ Q ∖ V. Then ρ := dist(z, V)/2 > 0 and j ≥ 1. Let φ(x) := max(0, 1 − |x − z|/ρ); it vanishes on V, and φ ≥ 1/2 on B(z, ρ/2).
 - For r > 0, η := η_{y,r} preserves V, so η(M') ∖ V = η(M' ∖ V), which has H^j-measure r^{−j}H^j(M' ∖ V) = 0.
 - Hence 0 ≤ ∫_{η(M')} φ dH^j ≤ H^j(η(M') ∖ V) = 0, and the tangent limit gives ∫_Q φ dH^j = 0.
 - This contradicts ∫_Q φ dH^j ≥ (1/2)H^j(Q ∩ B(z, ρ/2)) > 0, since H^j⌞Q is Lebesgue measure on Q.
I.3 (Product with a Borel subset of a frame span.) Let g be orthonormal (k vectors), G := span g, and k + m' = n'. Let E ⊆ G be Borel and A an IM m'-current with an IMRep R_A = (M_A, θ_A, ζ_A) such that μ_A(ℝ^P ∖ G^⊥) = 0. Then there is an IM n'-current [[E]] ×_g A, with an IMRep R_B, such that for every test n'-form ω and Borel C:
 ([[E]] ×_g A)(ω) = ∫_E A(♭_gω(t + ·)) dH^k(t) and R_B.measure(C) = ∫_E μ_A(C − t) dH^k(t).
 Proof. Write q_G := (G^⊥).starProjection and ι(a) := Σ_i a_ig_i, an isometry ℝ^k → G.
 (a) Reduction. H^{m'}(M_A ∖ G^⊥) ≤ μ_A(ℝ^P ∖ G^⊥) = 0. Replace M_A by M_A ∩ G^⊥; action, measure and all blow-up integrals (hence approximate tangent spaces) are unchanged. By I.2 (V = G^⊥), for H^{m'}-a.e. y ∈ M_A the approximate tangent space T_y oriented by ζ_A(y) satisfies T_y ⊆ G^⊥.
 (b) Product formula for H^{n'} (PM). For Borel E ⊆ G, Borel M ⊆ G^⊥ countably m'-rectifiable and locally H^{m'}-finite, and Borel g ≥ 0:
 ∫_{E+M} g dH^{n'} = ∫_E ∫_M g(t + y) dH^{m'}(y) dH^k(t), where E + M = p_G⁻¹(E) ∩ q_G⁻¹(M) is Borel.
 - Null part: if H^{m'}(N) = 0 then H^{n'}(E + N) = 0. By σ-additivity let E lie in a cube of side ℓ in G. Cover N by sets C_i of positive diameters < δ ≤ 1 with Σ_i (diam C_i)^{m'} < ε; enlarge degenerate sets slightly, keeping the sum < ε. Cover the cube by ≤ (ℓ/diam C_i + 1)^k subcubes of side diam C_i; each subcube plus C_i has diameter ≤ (√k + 1) diam C_i. Hence the H^{n'}_{(√k+1)δ}-premeasure of E + N is ≤ c Σ_i (ℓ^k (diam C_i)^{m'} + (diam C_i)^{n'}) ≤ c(ℓ^k + 1)ε. Let ε → 0, then δ → 0.
 - Rectifiable part: cover M up to an H^{m'}-null set by disjoint Borel images Φ_l(T_l), with Φ_l Lipschitz and injective on T_l (bi-Lipschitz pieces via Mathlib exists_partition_approximatesLinearOn_of_hasFDerivWithinAt, with tolerance c_A/2 for injective A and 1 otherwise; Lusin–Souslin; SimonGMT area_image_compl_regularSet_eq_zero). Replace Φ_l by q_G∘Φ_l, which equals Φ_l on T_l and has values in G^⊥.
 - G_l(a, u) := ι(a) + Φ_l(u) on ℝ^k × ℝ^{m'} is Lipschitz and injective on ι⁻¹E × T_l. At a.e. point DG_l = [ι | DΦ_l(u)] with range DΦ_l(u) ⊆ G^⊥ ⊥ G, so its Gram matrix is diag(I, DΦ_l*DΦ_l) and JG_l = JΦ_l.
 - The area formula for G_l and Φ_l, Tonelli, summation over l and the null part give (PM).
 (c) The product IMRep R_B. Put M_B := E + M_A, θ_B := θ_A∘q_G and ξ_B(x)(α) := ζ_A(q_G x)(♭_gα).
 - M_B is countably n'-rectifiable: covered by E + N and the Lipschitz images G_l(ℝ^{n'}).
 - θ_B ≥ 1 on M_B and θ_B is locally integrable: by (PM), ∫_{M_B∩K} θ_B ≤ H^k(p_GK)·∫_{M_A∩q_GK} θ_A < ∞.
 - ξ_B is a.e.-strongly measurable: compose a Borel version of ζ_A with q_G and ♭_g; the exceptional set is null by (PM).
 - Tangent planes. Let x = t + y with t a Lebesgue density point of E (in G) and y ∈ M_A having T_y ⊆ G^⊥. Then η_{x,r}(M_B) = η_{t,r}(E) + η_{y,r}(M_A). By (PM), for φ ∈ C_c with spt φ ⊆ B_ρ, ∫_{η_{x,r}(M_B)} φ = ∫_{η_{t,r}E} Φ_r(s) dH^k(s) with Φ_r(s) := ∫_{η_{y,r}M_A} φ(s + z) dH^{m'}(z). As r ↓ 0:
  - Φ_r(s) → ∫_{T_y} φ(s + z) dH^{m'}(z) for each s;
  - |Φ_r(s)| ≤ ‖φ‖_∞ H^{m'}(η_{y,r}M_A ∩ B_ρ) is bounded and vanishes for |s| ≥ ρ, because |s + z|² = |s|² + |z|²;
  - 1_{η_{t,r}E} → 1_G in L¹_loc(G).
  Dominated convergence gives the limit ∫_G ∫_{T_y} φ(s + z) = ∫_{G⊕T_y} φ dH^{n'}, by (PM) for subspaces. So M_B has approximate tangent space G ⊕ T_y at x (finrank k + m' = n').
 - Orientation. If ζ_A(y) = ±(β ↦ β(τ)) with τ an orthonormal basis of T_y, then ξ_B(x)(α) = ±α(Fin.append g τ ∘ Fin.cast h), and Fin.append g τ is an orthonormal basis of G ⊕ T_y. The bad x (t not a density point, or y bad) lie in (Z_E + M_A) ∪ (E + Z_A) with Z_E, Z_A Borel null sets, which is H^{n'}-null by (PM).
 - So R_B := (M_B, θ_B, ξ_B) is an IMRep. Let [[E]] ×_g A be a current it represents (F7).
 (d) Formulas. By (PM) applied to θ_B1_C, R_B.measure(C) = ∫_E μ_A(C − t) dt. For the action, the integrand θ_Bξ_B(ω) is integrable, being bounded by θ_B‖ω‖_∞1_{tsupport ω}. By (PM) on its positive and negative parts,
 R_B.action(ω) = ∫_E ∫_{M_A} θ_Aζ_A(♭_gω(t + y)) dH^{m'}(y) dt = ∫_E A(♭_gω(t + ·)) dt. ∎(I.3)

PART II. The comparison.
1. (Integer multiplicity.) S₀ is represented by R₀, so it is integer multiplicity. By (F6c), spt S₀ ⊆ L^⊥, since μ₀ vanishes on the open set ℝ^P ∖ L^⊥.
2. (A competitor and the defect δ.) Let W₀, S₀' be as in the conclusion, with K₀ := spt(S₀' − S₀) compact and K₀ ⊆ L^⊥ ∩ W₀. As m ≥ 1, SameBoundary means ∂S₀' = ∂S₀ = 0. By (F1), M_{W₀}(S₀) = μ₀(W₀) ≤ μ₀(cl W₀) < ∞. Suppose, for contradiction, that M_{W₀}(S₀') < M_{W₀}(S₀), and put δ := M_{W₀}(S₀) − M_{W₀}(S₀') ∈ (0, ∞).
3. (The cycle X₀ and its cone Y₀.)
 - X₀ := S₀' − S₀ is IM by (F4), with ∂X₀ = 0, spt X₀ = K₀ compact and K₀ ⊆ L^⊥.
 - By cone_filling_subspace (V = L^⊥), there is an IM Y₀ ∈ 𝒟_{m+1}(ℝ^P) with ∂Y₀ = X₀, spt Y₀ compact and spt Y₀ ⊆ L^⊥.
 - M(Y₀) = μ_{Y₀}(ℝ^P) = μ_{Y₀}(spt Y₀) < ∞, by (F1) and (F6b).
 - Concentration. spt S₀' ⊆ spt S₀ ∪ K₀ ⊆ L^⊥: if a test form vanishes near spt S₀ ∪ K₀, then S₀ and X₀ vanish on it by (F6a). So by (F6b), μ_{S₀'}, μ_{X₀} and μ_{Y₀} vanish off L^⊥.
4. (Products used.)
 - With g = f (k = d): for Borel E ⊆ L and A ∈ {S₀, S₀', X₀} (m' = m, n' = n), and for A = Y₀ (m' = m + 1, n' = n + 1, no degree cast needed), I.3 gives IM currents [[E]] × A := [[E]] ×_f A with ([[E]] × A)(ω) = ∫_E A(♭_fω(t + ·)) dt and μ_{[[E]]×A}(C) = ∫_E μ_A(C − t) dt.
 - Faces. For a ∈ {1, …, d} let f^{(a)} := (f_1, …, f̂_a, …, f_d), orthonormal, with span L_a, dim d − 1, and L^⊥ ⊆ L_a^⊥. I.3 with g = f^{(a)}, k = d − 1 and m' = m + 1 (n' = n) gives [[E]] ×_a Y₀ for Borel E ⊆ L_a, with M([[E]] ×_a Y₀) = H^{d−1}(E)·M(Y₀) (F1 on ℝ^P). For d = 1 the frame is empty, E = {0}, and the product is Y₀ itself.
5. (Boundary of the cube product.) For r > 0 let:
 - Q_r := {t ∈ L : |t^a| ≤ r ∀a}, with H^d(Q_r) = (2r)^d;
 - Q'_a := {Σ_{b≠a} s^bf_b : |s^b| ≤ r} ⊆ L_a, with H^{d−1}(Q'_a) = (2r)^{d−1};
 - P_a := [[Q'_a]] ×_a Y₀.
 Define E'_r := Σ_{a=1}^d (−1)^{a−1}(τ_{rf_a}P_a − τ_{−rf_a}P_a). It is IM by (F4) and translation, and M(E'_r) ≤ Σ_a 2M(P_a) = 2d(2r)^{d−1}M(Y₀).
 Claim: ∂([[Q_r]] × Y₀) = E'_r + (−1)^d [[Q_r]] × X₀.
 Proof. Let ω be a test n-form and ♭ := ♭_f on Λ^{n+1} (m' = m + 1). Use dω(x)(v_0, …, v_n) = Σ_i (−1)^i Dω(x)[v_i](…v̂_i…) (SimonGMT exteriorDerivative_apply) with v = (f_1, …, f_d, w_1, …, w_{m+1}). For every x and w:
 ♭(dω(x))(w) = Σ_a (−1)^{a−1} D_{f_a}[♭_{f^{(a)}}ω](x)(w) + (−1)^d d(♭_fω)(x)(w).
 The terms with v_i = f_a (i = a − 1) give the first sum. The terms with v_i = w_j (i = d + j − 1) give (−1)^{d+j−1}D_{w_j}[♭_fω](x)(ŵ_j), and Σ_j (−1)^{j−1}D_{w_j}[♭_fω](x)(ŵ_j) = d(♭_fω)(x)(w). Integrate over Q_r:
 - Second term: d(♭_fω)(t + ·) = d[♭_fω(t + ·)] and Y₀(dγ) = (∂Y₀)(γ) = X₀(γ), giving (−1)^d([[Q_r]] × X₀)(ω).
 - First term: g_a(t) := Y₀(♭_{f^{(a)}}ω(t + ·)) is C¹ with ∂_{t^a}g_a(t) = Y₀(D_{f_a}[♭_{f^{(a)}}ω](t + ·)): difference quotients of t ↦ ♭_{f^{(a)}}ω(t + ·) converge in the test-form topology, and Y₀ is continuous. By Fubini in the coordinates t^b and the fundamental theorem of calculus in t^a,
 ∫_{Q_r} ∂_{t^a}g_a dt = ∫_{Q'_a} [g_a(s + rf_a) − g_a(s − rf_a)] dH^{d−1}(s) = (τ_{rf_a}P_a)(ω) − (τ_{−rf_a}P_a)(ω).
 Summing gives ([[Q_r]] × Y₀)(dω) = E'_r(ω) + (−1)^d([[Q_r]] × X₀)(ω).
6. (The competitor for S.) Put Z_r := (−1)^d ∂([[Q_r]] × Y₀) = [[Q_r]] × X₀ + (−1)^d E'_r (step 5).
 - Z_r is IM, by (F4).
 - ∂Z_r = 0, since ∂∂ = 0 (CurrentOn.boundary_boundary).
 - spt Z_r ⊆ spt([[Q_r]] × Y₀) ⊆ Q_r + spt Y₀. The measure of [[Q_r]] × Y₀ vanishes off the closed set Q_r + spt Y₀ (I.3 and (F6b)); then apply (F6c), and use that the support of a boundary lies in the support.
 Choose an open ball B = B_ρ(0) ⊇ cl(W₀) ∪ spt Y₀ (compact). Let C_{r+1} := {t ∈ L : |t^a| < r + 1 ∀a} and W := {x : p(x) ∈ C_{r+1}, q(x) ∈ B}.
 - W is open, and cl W ⊆ {x : |t^a(x)| ≤ r + 1, |q x| ≤ ρ} is compact.
 - spt Z_r ⊆ Q_r + spt Y₀ ⊆ W, since spt Y₀ ⊆ B ∩ L^⊥.
 Let S' := S + Z_r. It is IM (F4); ∂S' = ∂S (n ≥ 2, boundary linear); and S' − S = Z_r, so spt(S' − S) is a compact subset of W = univ ∩ W. Minimality of S gives:
 (MIN) M_W(S) ≤ M_W(S').
7. (Mass of S.) For t ∈ L and y ∈ L^⊥, t + y ∈ W iff t ∈ C_{r+1} and y ∈ B. Hence μ₀(W − t) = 1_{C_{r+1}}(t)μ₀(B), by concentration on L^⊥. By (F1) and the measure identity,
 M_W(S) = μ(W) = ∫_L μ₀(W − t) dt = (2r + 2)^d μ₀(B).
8. (Mass of S'.) For a test n-form ω, the function t ↦ S₀(♭_fω(t + ·)) is continuous and vanishes unless t ∈ p(tsupport ω), by (F6a) and spt S₀ ⊆ L^⊥; so it is integrable. With S₀' = S₀ + X₀:
 (S + [[Q_r]] × X₀)(ω) = ∫_L S₀(♭_fω(t + ·)) dt + ∫_{Q_r} X₀(♭_fω(t + ·)) dt = ∫_{L∖Q_r} S₀(♭_fω(t + ·)) dt + ∫_{Q_r} S₀'(♭_fω(t + ·)) dt.
 Hence S' = [[L ∖ Q_r]] × S₀ + [[Q_r]] × S₀' + (−1)^d E'_r. By subadditivity, (F1) and step 4, as in step 7:
 M_W(S') ≤ μ_{[[L∖Q_r]]×S₀}(W) + μ_{[[Q_r]]×S₀'}(W) + M(E'_r)
 ≤ ((2r + 2)^d − (2r)^d)μ₀(B) + (2r)^d μ_{S₀'}(B) + 2d(2r)^{d−1}M(Y₀).
9. (Comparing μ_{S₀'} and μ₀.) On the open set U' := ℝ^P ∖ K₀, S₀' and S₀ agree: (S₀' − S₀)(γ) = 0 if tsupport γ ⊆ U', by (F6a) for X₀.
 - Restrict a representation R' of S₀' and R₀ to U': carriers ∩ U', same mult and orient. These are IMReps in U': Borel, rectifiable, locally integrable, and approximate tangent spaces at points of the open set U' are unchanged.
 - Both represent the restricted current, so by (F3), μ_{S₀'}(C) = μ₀(C) for Borel C ⊆ U'.
 - As K₀ ⊆ W₀ ⊆ B, and using (F1) for W₀:
 μ_{S₀'}(B) − μ₀(B) = μ_{S₀'}(K₀) − μ₀(K₀) = μ_{S₀'}(W₀) − μ₀(W₀) = M_{W₀}(S₀') − M_{W₀}(S₀) = −δ.
 All these quantities are finite.
10. (Contradiction.) By steps 7–9,
 M_W(S') − M_W(S) ≤ −δ(2r)^d + 2d(2r)^{d−1}M(Y₀) = (2r)^{d−1}(2d M(Y₀) − 2rδ) < 0
 for r > d M(Y₀)/δ. This contradicts (MIN). Hence M_{W₀}(S₀) ≤ M_{W₀}(S₀') for all such competitors, and with step 1, S₀ is minimizing in L^⊥. ∎
proof_key_steps: Tools: the interior product ♭_g with an orthonormal frame, tangent planes inside a subspace, and the IM product [[E]] ×_g A (E ⊆ span g, A concentrated on (span g)^⊥) with product measure, via the Hausdorff product formula and dtc_imrep_current.
A competitor S₀' with smaller mass in W₀ gives an IM cycle X₀ = S₀' − S₀ in L^⊥ ∩ W₀; cone_filling_subspace gives Y₀ with ∂Y₀ = X₀ and spt Y₀ ⊆ L^⊥.
Stokes in each t^a gives ∂([[Q_r]] × Y₀) = E'_r + (−1)^d[[Q_r]] × X₀, with E'_r the face terms of mass ≤ 2d(2r)^{d−1}M(Y₀).
S' := S + (−1)^d∂([[Q_r]] × Y₀) = [[L∖Q_r]] × S₀ + [[Q_r]] × S₀' + (−1)^d E'_r is an admissible competitor in the box W.
Mass bookkeeping with M_W = μ(W) gives M_W(S') − M_W(S) ≤ −δ(2r)^d + 2d(2r)^{d−1}M(Y₀) < 0 for large r, contradicting minimality of S.

subproblem.title: A translation-invariant integer multiplicity current whose tangent planes contain L is a product: S = [[L]] × S₀ with S₀ supported in L^⊥
subproblem.statement:
Data:
- P, n ∈ ℕ; L ⊆ ℝ^P a linear subspace with 1 ≤ d := dim L < n; m := n − d.
- f = (f_1, …, f_d) an orthonormal family in L (hence an orthonormal basis of L).
- S ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) and an integer multiplicity representation R = (M, θ, ξ) of S (IMRep univ n, R.Represents S); μ := R.measure.
Hypotheses:
- S is invariant under translations by L: currentEval (blowUp S (−v) 1) ω = S ω, i.e. S(ω(v + ·)) = S(ω), for v ∈ L and ω ∈ 𝒟^n(ℝ^P).
- For μ-a.e. x, the projection p_x onto approxTangentPlane n M x fixes every v ∈ L.
Conclusion: there are S₀ ∈ 𝒟_m(ℝ^P) and an integer multiplicity representation R₀ of S₀ (IMRep univ m) such that:
- spt S₀ ⊆ L^⊥;
- μ₀ := R₀.measure satisfies μ₀(ℝ^P ∖ L^⊥) = 0;
- μ(A) = ∫_L μ₀(A − t) dH^d(t) for every Borel A, written ∫⁻ t in L, μ₀((fun y => t + y)⁻¹' A) ∂μHE[d];
- product formula: let ♭ : Λ^n → Λ^m be any map with (♭α)(v) = α(f_1, …, f_d, v_1, …, v_m) (Lean: α (Fin.append f v ∘ Fin.cast _)). Then for every test n-form ω,
 S(ω) = ∫_L currentEval S₀ (y ↦ ♭(ω(t + y))) dH^d(t).

subproblem.natural_proof:
Notation. p := L.starProjection and q := I − p = Lᗮ.starProjection. H^k := μHE[k]; on k-dimensional subspaces it is Lebesgue measure. M_t := M ∩ p⁻¹(t) for t ∈ L. "IMRep" means an IMRep univ of the stated dimension. Let ♭ be a map as in the statement.
Accepted declarations used (DAG reuse siblings):
- dtc_imrep_current: every IMRep defines a current that it represents.
- imrep_weighted_orient_indicator_ae_eq: two representations of one current in an open set have H^n-a.e. equal data 1_M θ ξ on the union of their carriers.
- imrep_measure_eq_of_represents_same_current: two representations of one current have the same measure.
Child used: spine_coarea.
1. (♭ is the interior product.) The defining identity determines ♭α. Hence ♭(α + β) = ♭α + ♭β and ♭(cα) = c♭α; evaluate at each v. Also ‖♭α‖ ≤ ‖α‖, since f is orthonormal. So ♭ is continuous linear. For every test n-form ω and t ∈ ℝ^P, the form y ↦ ♭(ω(t + y)) is C^∞ with tsupport ⊆ tsupport ω − t, compact; it is a test m-form, so currentEval S₀ of it equals S₀ applied to it.
2. (Lift.) There is a continuous linear lift : Λ^m → Λ^n with (lift β)(f_1, …, f_d, w_1, …, w_m) = β(w_1, …, w_m) for all w_j ∈ L^⊥. Equivalently, (♭(lift β))(w) = β(w) for w ∈ (L^⊥)^m.
 Construction: (lift β)(v_1, …, v_n) := (1/m!) Σ_{σ∈S_n} sgn(σ) ∏_{a=1}^d ⟨f_a, v_{σ(a)}⟩ · β(q v_{σ(d+1)}, …, q v_{σ(n)}), the alternatization (Mathlib MultilinearMap.alternatization) of a multilinear map.
 Evaluation at (f, w) with w_j ∈ L^⊥: a term is nonzero only if v_{σ(a)} = f_a for every a ≤ d, because ⟨f_a, w_j⟩ = 0 and ⟨f_a, f_b⟩ = δ_ab. So σ fixes 1, …, d. The remaining sum is Σ_{π∈S_m} sgn(π) β(w_π) = m! β(w).
3. (Orientation decomposition.)
 - Borel version of ξ. Let ξ̃ be Borel with ξ̃ = ξ H^n⌞M-a.e. (AEStronglyMeasurable.mk). R̃ := (M, θ, ξ̃) is an IMRep representing S with R̃.measure = μ; the integrands of the action agree a.e.
 - The good set G. Let G be the set of x ∈ M such that:
  - ξ̃(x) = ξ(x);
